title: This Button Has Done Nothing Since 1990
description: You press 'close door' in the lift, the button at the crossing and the office thermostat. Most of them do nothing. Ryan finds out why: the 1990 lift law, New York's 2,500 placebo crossing buttons, London's daytime crossings, the dummy thermostats contractors admit to, the click your phone fakes, the noise electric cars must make, the illusion of control, and the sugar pills that work even when you know.

seo.title: This Button Does Nothing. So Why Do We Keep Pressing It?
seo.description: Ever wonder why useless buttons feel so satisfying to press? We dive into the hidden psychology of placebo controls, from ADA door closers to dummy thermostats, revealing how your brain manufactures control out of nothing. From fake camera clicks to expensive sugar pills, discover why these harmless illusions shape our habits and prove that perception often matters more than reality.
